calls.head: Where the Islanders have the edge: depth
calls.body: The Islanders are one of the league’s best for depth, and the Blackhawks are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Blackhawks.

calls.head: The Blackhawks’ edge in the penalty kill
calls.body: The Blackhawks are around the middle of the league for the penalty kill, and the Islanders are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Blackhawks’ penalty kill allows less per 60 than the Islanders’.

surprises.head: The Islanders got the good looks
surprises.body: The Islanders’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.2% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Islanders take down the Blackhawks
paras: Bo Horvat opened the scoring for the Islanders on the power play late in the first. Emil Heineman and Anthony Duclair scored 2:54 apart midway through the second to stretch the lead to 3-0. Frank Nazar got the Blackhawks on the board on the power play with the goalie pulled with 2:34 left. Horvat struck again with 1:33 left into the empty net with 1:33 left.
The chances were closer than the score. Ilya Sorokin made 22 saves for the Islanders, and Arvid Söderblom stopped 15 of 18.

Nazar was thrown out with a match penalty in the final minutes. Tyler Bertuzzi and Logan Stanley picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Islanders improved to 2-2-0, and the Blackhawks dropped to 1-4-0.
